_about: Every document or value that writes `expires_at` or `purge_after` under src/ (tests/support/ttl_registry.py scans for writers; tests/unit/test_ttl_registry.py). deleted_by: ttl-policy (a Firestore TTL policy, in the generated runbook of docs/07_deployment/README.md), janitor, never, unverified (the code says a policy is meant, the runbook lists none), provider, not-stored. prefixed:false = the collection-group id carries no environment prefix; runbook_also / runbook_row=merged put two groups in one runbook row.

entries.note: a fact's expiry is a decision: the janitor stales the fact, never deletes it; no TTL policy, ever (tests/unit/test_facts_have_no_ttl_policy.py)

entries.what_expires: tickets, the one-call marker, call-kind keys, late-answer records
long-turn registry records
unsaved skill drafts (30 days) and their staged file contents
staged file contents of unsaved skill drafts
entries.note: an unprefixed subcollection group (never `files`), keyed by collection-group across the database (firestore_skill_repository.py `_DRAFT_FILES`); its runbook row is merged into skill_drafts

entries.what_expires: unconfirmed memory-fact drafts (7 days)
Cloud Tasks claims (1 h), daily-review marks (48 h), external task API per-worker rate windows (two windows after the window starts)
monthly drive model-usage documents (the `{user}:initial` document has no `expires_at`)
server-side integration connect flows (10 minutes); the ephemeral store reads the expiry itself, the policy only sweeps abandoned flows
one-time `$geo` location links (10 minutes); the ephemeral store reads the expiry itself, the policy only sweeps unused links
inbound event dedup claims (1 h); reads check expiry themselves
pending passkey ceremonies (5 minutes, single use); the ephemeral store reads the expiry itself, the policy only sweeps abandoned ones
pending drive-note erase requests
short links (`resolve` re-checks expiry itself, the sweep lags)

entries.note: expiry is checked when a code is redeemed; nothing deletes the document

entries.what_expires: MCP authorization codes (about 10 minutes)
expired MCP refresh tokens (an absent token is refused like an expired one)

entries.note: `expires_at` is written and never read; expiry is a lazy 90-day check in `load_session`; no TTL policy
the expiry of a Microsoft Graph webhook subscription inside the task-config document; the renewal tick replaces it, nothing deletes it
read-checked (a link dies 5 minutes after issue); the record is deleted by the `purge_after` policy

entries.what_expires: ended or expired Cabinet device sessions (the record is kept for a grace period after its absolute end or its revocation)

entries.note: the session's absolute end, checked on read (`is_live`, refresh); the record is deleted by the `purge_after` policy
when the model provider drops an uploaded input file; not a document of ours
in-memory values: a provider token's expiry, a prompt cache's expiry, a voice token's `exp` claim; the Cabinet access token's `exp` claim

entries.what_expires: closed memory-review questions (90 days after closing; an open question has no `purge_after`)
weekly-digest claims (90 days after the claim) and quote translations (180 days after they were written)
cached transcripts of opened chat audio (90 days after they were written; chat uploads themselves are deleted after 30 days by the bucket lifecycle)
the drive connector's one-time download links (a day after issue; a link itself dies 5 minutes after issue, checked on read)
external task records (30 days after the task reaches a final state; a task still open has no `purge_after`)
the stored result text of a done external task (30 days after the task is done, the same instant as its task record)
